newsitem.title: ITALY: Stet, Seat committee discuss accounts.
newsitem.headline: Stet, Seat committee discuss accounts.

text.p: An advisory committee nominated by Italian telecoms holding Stet and its former yellow pages unit Seat on Monday recommended that Seat's accounts should include a 109 billion lire net benefit relating to the spin-off.
The Treasury said in a statement the committee's decision had not yet been evaluated by the board of either company.

The committee was charged with assessing the size of the spin-off settlement, with regard to the problems of Seat's loss-making Multi Media Publicita unit, which is to be wound up, and other balance-sheet considerations.
Seat's board will meet on June 25 to assess how much cash should be set aside in the accounts to cover the liquidation costs of MMP, which lost more than 180 billion lire in 1996.
The Treasury owns Stet, which is being merged with its main operating unit Telecom Italia and is due to be privatised later this year.
Seat is also up for sale after being spun off from Stet. The Treasury has given potential bidders until the end of this month to put in final offers for the company.
